original.goal: Roleplay workplace scenarios to practice adapting your communication style, showing respect, and fitting into U.S. business culture.
original.title: Practicing Respect & Adaptability in Conversations
original.body_en:
🤝 Speaking Practice

Title: Practicing Respect & Adaptability in Conversations
Time: 2 hours
Objective: Roleplay workplace scenarios to practice adapting your communication style, showing respect, and fitting into U.S. business culture.

Activity 1: Small Talk at Work (10–15 min)

Pair with a classmate, colleague, or even practice with a friend/family member.

One person plays the role of a coworker, the other introduces themselves and starts a short workplace-friendly conversation.

Prompts:

"Hi, I'm [Name]. I just joined the [Department]. What projects are you working on?"

"How long have you been with the company?"

"What do you enjoy about working here?"

⚡ Focus: Keep it polite, light, and professional. Avoid overly personal questions.

Activity 2: Asking for Clarification (15–20 min)

Roleplay a meeting situation where something isn't clear.

Scenario:

Partner plays the "manager" giving instructions.

You practice asking for clarification in a respectful way.

❌ Don't say: "That makes no sense."
✅ Say: "I want to make sure I understood correctly. Could you walk me through that step again?"

⚡ Focus: Stay calm, direct, and professional.

Activity 3: Giving & Receiving Feedback (20–25 min)

Partner plays your teammate.

Practice giving constructive feedback.

Example:

❌ "This report is wrong."

✅ "I think this section could be clearer if we added more data. What do you think?"

Then switch roles. Practice receiving feedback without being defensive:

"Thanks for pointing that out. I'll adjust it."

⚡ Focus: Solution-oriented tone.

Activity 4: Difficult Conversation (20–25 min)

Scenario: You are behind schedule on a project. Your boss (partner) asks why.

❌ "It's not my fault."
✅ "I've run into delays with X, but I'm reorganizing priorities so we stay on track. I'd also appreciate your feedback."

⚡ Focus: Honesty + accountability + solutions.

Self-Reflection Prompt

After finishing the roleplays, answer out loud (or write):

Which situation felt easiest?

Which one challenged you most?

How will you adjust your tone and clarity next time?

Why This Matters:

These speaking drills mirror real U.S. workplace interactions. The more you practice, the more natural respectful, direct, and confident communication will feel in English.

👉 Practice these at least twice this week, and if possible, record one of your roleplays to evaluate yourself.
original.body_es:
🤝 Práctica de Conversación

Título: Practicando Respeto y Adaptabilidad en Conversaciones
Tiempo: 2 horas
Objetivo: Representar escenarios laborales para practicar la adaptación de tu estilo de comunicación, mostrar respeto e integrarte en la cultura empresarial de EE.UU.

Actividad 1: Charla Informal en el Trabajo (10–15 min)

Empareja con un compañero de clase, colega, o incluso practica con un amigo/familiar.

Una persona juega el papel de un compañero de trabajo, la otra se presenta y comienza una breve conversación adecuada para el lugar de trabajo.

Sugerencias:

"Hi, I'm [Name]. I just joined the [Department]. What projects are you working on?"

"How long have you been with the company?"

"What do you enjoy about working here?"

⚡ Enfoque: Mantén la conversación educada, ligera y profesional. Evita preguntas demasiado personales.

Actividad 2: Pidiendo Aclaraciones (15–20 min)

Representa una situación de reunión donde algo no está claro.

Escenario:

Tu compañero juega el papel del "gerente" dando instrucciones.

Practica pedir aclaraciones de manera respetuosa.

❌ No digas: "That makes no sense."
✅ Di: "I want to make sure I understood correctly. Could you walk me through that step again?"

⚡ Enfoque: Mantente calmado, directo y profesional.

Actividad 3: Dar y Recibir Retroalimentación (20–25 min)

Tu compañero juega el papel de tu compañero de equipo.

Practica dar retroalimentación constructiva.

Ejemplo:

❌ "This report is wrong."

✅ "I think this section could be clearer if we added more data. What do you think?"

Luego cambia de roles. Practica recibir retroalimentación sin ponerte a la defensiva:

"Thanks for pointing that out. I'll adjust it."

⚡ Enfoque: Tono orientado a soluciones.

Actividad 4: Conversación Difícil (20–25 min)

Escenario: Estás atrasado en un proyecto. Tu jefe (compañero) pregunta por qué.

❌ "It's not my fault."
✅ "I've run into delays with X, but I'm reorganizing priorities so we stay on track. I'd also appreciate your feedback."

⚡ Enfoque: Honestidad + responsabilidad + soluciones.

Pregunta de Autorreflexión

Después de terminar las representaciones, responde en voz alta (o escribe):

¿Cuál situación te resultó más fácil?

¿Cuál te desafió más?

¿Cómo ajustarás tu tono y claridad la próxima vez?

Por Qué Esto Importa:

Estos ejercicios de conversación reflejan interacciones reales en el lugar de trabajo en EE.UU. Cuanto más practiques, más natural te parecerá comunicarte de manera respetuosa, directa y segura en inglés.

👉 Practica esto al menos dos veces esta semana, y si es posible, graba una de tus representaciones para evaluarte a ti mismo.
